scenes.name: New Order
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Los supervivientes de Joy Division, perdidos tras la muerte de Curtis («Ceremony», Movement), echan a Martin Hannett, aprenden a programar cajas de ritmos con música electrónica italiana y descubren en Nueva York los clubes chic, la emisora Kiss FM, los remixes de Pettibone, el freestyle y el electro. «Everything's Gone Green» (1981) marca el giro; «Blue Monday» (1983) y «Confusion», producido por Arthur Baker, los convierten en una banda de baile. Con Factory abren The Haçienda, inspirada en Danceteria y Funhouse.

podcast.title: "Blue Monday" Composition & Accidental Rest
podcast.body: As keyboardist for New Order, Gillian Gilbert meticulously wrote out the entire sequence for "Blue Monday" by hand on paper. She accidentally included an extra rest in her notation, causing her program to be slightly out of time, but this "mistake" was intentionally kept for the extra tension it added to the arrangement. "Meanwhile, Jillian Gilbert, the keyboardist, wrote out the entire sequence by hand on paper. However, she accidentally added an extra rest in her notation, which made her program slightly out of time with everything else."

podcast.title: Synthesizer Automation
podcast.body: Gillian Gilbert's synthesizers became an integral part of New Order's evolving electronic setup. A sequencer was used to automate keyboard parts and trigger sounds on her synthesizers, contributing to the band's distinctive new sound. "had it trigger something on Jillian Gilbert synthesizers."

xref.title: Gillian and Steven's Marriage (1994)
xref.body: Gillian Gilbert and Steven Morris started dating before she was asked to join New Order, and they officially married in 1994. "They started dating even before she was asked to join the band and finally made it official with a wedding in 1994."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Accident of Laziness" Origin of Dance Sound
xref.body: New Order's groundbreaking electronic sound and worldwide alt-rock influence partly originated from their reluctance to perform encores. They initially played Stephen Morris's drum machine alone as they left the stage, later adding a sequencer for Gillian Gilbert's synthesizers, and finally, Bernard Sumner conceived sequencing Peter Hook's bass line, leading to songs performed largely by machines. "But their worldwide success and the way they changed alt rock forever was due to an accident of laziness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Blue Monday" Composition & Instrumentation
xref.body: The composition of "Blue Monday" involved a complex setup: a sequencer built by Stephen Morris connected to an Emulator sampler, a Moog Source keyboard for the bass line, and an Oberheim DMX drum machine. Engineer Martin Usher wrote code to synchronize these devices, and keyboardist Gillian Gilbert's accidental inclusion of an extra rest in her handwritten notation was deliberately kept for the added tension it brought to the arrangement. "He built a sequencer that could be connected to the band's new sampler, a keyboard called an emulator. They sampled a choral effect from a craftwork song called Uranium and wrote a bass line using another keyboard called a Mogue source."

xref.title: Gillian Gilbert Joining (Synthesizers)
xref.body: The band's sound significantly changed when Steven Morris's girlfriend, Gillian Gilbert, joined on synthesizers. Gillian had been a fan of Joy Division and was in her own band, The Inadequates, before joining New Order. "But that all changed when Steven's girlfriend, that's Jillian, joined unsynthesizers. She'd been a fan of Jordy Vision and had her own band called The Inadequates."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Gillian's Hiatus for Daughter's Health
xref.body: Gillian Gilbert took a 10-year break from New Order to dedicate more time to one of their daughters, who was suffering from a serious neurological condition. "And Jillian bowed out of New Order for 10 years so she could spend more time with one of their daughters who suffered from a serious neurological condition."
